verdict.rationale: The core DBOS library is explicitly open-source and self-hostable with no proprietary server — it runs as a library backed only by Postgres, confirmed by docs and GitHub ('no separate orchestration server and no infrastructure required besides Postgres'), and docs explicitly contrast this with hosted orchestrators like Temporal. Community comments corroborate this lightweight self-hosted architecture (co-founder describes it running 'inside your program' with just DB writes). Some caveats exist around the optional Conductor/dashboard UI not being fully open-sourced yet (per community complaint), but that is an add-on, not the core library. Missing for 10: independent hands-on verification of a full self-hosted production deployment, and clarity on whether Conductor console self-hosting is fully open-source today.
